```python
    return {"hello": "world"}


app = Starlite(route_handlers=[hello_world], debug=True)
```

I have investigated the issue where stringized return annotations (due to `from __future__ import annotations` or explicit string annotations) caused OpenAPI to generate a "no-content" response because the return type was not being resolved.

The issue lies in `starlite/_signature/parsing.py`, where `parse_fn_signature` uses `signature.return_annotation` directly from the `inspect.Signature` object. Unlike function parameters, which are processed using `get_fn_type_hints` (which resolves stringified annotations using the provided namespace), the return annotation is taken as-is from the signature.

To fix this, I have updated `parse_fn_signature` to use `get_fn_type_hints` to resolve the return annotation using the same `signature_namespace` used for parameters. This ensures that stringified annotations are correctly de-stringized.

```python
starlite/_signature/parsing.py::parse_fn_signature
```

I changed the return line of `parse_fn_signature` to use the resolved type hints for the return annotation.

```python
+    return parsed_params, fn_type_hints.get("return", signature.return_annotation), field_plugin_mappings, dependency_names
```
